communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the North Carolina Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

To the Custodian of Records, Wake County Sheriff's Office:

Under the North Carolina Public Records Act, N.C.G.S. Section 132-1 et seq., I request the following existing records, in the public interest and not for any commercial purpose.

I request the facility's daily jail booking log (booking register / arrest blotter) for every individual booked into the Wake County Detention Center from January 1, 2025 to the present. For each booking, I request the existing fields your jail-management system already records:

1. Booking or system number;
2. Name;
3. Date and time of booking;
4. Date of release;
5. The charge(s) or hold(s) associated with the booking, as recorded in the charges field;
6. Arresting or committing agency;
7. Warrant or reference number.

This is the facility's routine booking log -- ordinary public booking information -- and I request it in the existing electronic format your jail-management system exports (a spreadsheet, CSV, or delimited file is preferred; I do not require a formatted report). N.C.G.S. Section 132-6.2 provides that public records maintained in electronic form shall be made available in electronic form. Producing an export or query of data already maintained in your system is retrieval of an existing record, not the creation of a new one.

This request is not a duplicate of Records Request No. 26-3175, which concerned a narrower subject and was closed without production of any booking log; this request seeks the Office's general booking log for all bookings in the period, a different and broader record. The booking log is the Office's own jail record and the Office is its custodian. N.C.G.S. Section 132-6.2 provides that public records maintained in electronic form shall be made available in that form, and an agency may not decline to produce them because responding requires retrieving data from a database. I am requesting the existing booking data for all bookings in the period, in any export format your system supports.

As a public-interest, non-commercial request, I ask for a fee waiver or reduction; if a fee applies, please provide an itemized written estimate before incurring any cost, and I will respond promptly, including by narrowing the date range if that helps. If any portion is withheld, please state in writing the specific legal basis as N.C.G.S. Section 132-6(a) requires, and please preserve all responsive records pending resolution. Thank you.

Glen Wasserstein
(929) 786-1863

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Glen Wasserstein

records, in the public interest and not for any commercial purpose (research and public education
regarding local detention practices).

I request the Sheriff's Office **arrest and booking log** (the jail booking records the Office maintains
in the ordinary course) for every individual booked into the Harris County Jail from **January 1, 2025
to the present**. For each booking, I request the existing fields your jail-management system records,
including:

1. Booking or system (SPN/SO) number;
2. Name;
3. Date and time of booking/confinement;
4. Date of release;
5. The charge(s) or hold(s) associated with the booking, as recorded in the charges field (including any
   notation your system enters for a hold or detainer);
6. Arresting/committing agency;

your public inmate/booking search — and I request it in the existing electronic format your
jail-management system exports (a spreadsheet, CSV, or delimited file is preferred; I do not require a
formatted report). If producing it requires programming or manipulation of data, § 552.231 requires a
written statement of whether it can be produced, in what form, and the cost and time — and then
production; every jail-management system can export its booking log.

I do not seek any confidential criminal-history record. The state identification (SID) number and any DPS

communications.communication:
Dear FOIA Officer:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, I request records maintained by the U.S. Department of State, including the Bureau of Consular Affairs and the American Citizen Services section of the U.S. Embassy in London, concerning demand for services relating to formal renunciation of U.S. nationality under INA § 349(a)(5), 8 U.S.C. § 1481(a)(5).

**Date range:** January 1, 2024, through October 31, 2026.

I request existing reports, spreadsheets, databases, dashboards, statistical summaries, appointment-management records, and routinely generated exports containing any of the following information:

1. **Initial requests:** The number of individuals newly requesting renunciation appointments or joining a renunciation appointment waitlist, preferably broken down by calendar month.

2. **Waitlist size:** The number of individuals awaiting renunciation appointments, including any existing monthly or periodic snapshots of the waiting list.

3. **Appointment offers and scheduling:** The number of renunciation appointments offered, scheduled, cancelled, or rescheduled, preferably broken down by calendar month.

4. **Completed appointments:** The number of completed in-person renunciation appointments or oaths of renunciation, preferably broken down by calendar month.

5. **Waiting times:** Existing reports or summaries showing the time between an individual's initial appointment request or waitlist registration and the date an appointment was offered or held.

6. **Appointment capacity:** Existing statistical reports showing the number of renunciation appointment slots allocated or made available during the requested period.

The purpose of this request is to examine changes in demand and appointment processing before and after April 13, 2026, when the administrative processing fee for a Certificate of Loss of Nationality decreased from $2,350 to $450.

**Scope and format**

I seek existing records, not newly prepared statistical analyses. Where monthly aggregates are unavailable, please provide the closest available periodic reports or existing electronic tabular records containing the requested information.

I do not seek individuals' names, contact information, identification numbers, individual case files, or the contents of individual correspondence. If records contain personally identifiable information, please release reasonably segregable aggregate data or non-identifying fields.

Where available, please distinguish formal renunciations under INA § 349(a)(5) from other relinquishment requests under INA § 349(a)(1)–(4).

Please provide responsive records electronically, preferably in their native formats, including CSV or XLSX for tabular records.

If some requested categories are not maintained, please process the remaining categories independently rather than treating the request as indivisible. If clarification or narrowing would materially facilitate processing, please contact me before making an adverse determination.

**Fees and public interest**

This request is noncommercial. The information concerns public access to a federal consular service and the effects of a substantial change in government fees. I intend to make responsive records publicly available through MuckRock.

I request a waiver of applicable processing fees on public-interest grounds. If a waiver is denied, I agree to pay up to $25 in applicable fees and request advance notification before incurring any greater amount.

Please acknowledge receipt, assign a tracking number, and provide any records available for release on a rolling basis.

Thank you for your consideration,
Nicholas Lee

Please note it is unlawful to assign the task of e-mail searches to the e-mail custodians themselves.

Please search all records regarding agency business. You may not exclude searches of files or emails in the personal custody of your officials, such as personal email accounts or personal Skype accounts. Records of official business conducted using unofficial systems or stored outside of official files are subject to the Federal Records Act and FOIA. See Competitive Enter. Inst. v. Office of Sci. & Tech. Policy,  241 F. Supp. 3d 14, 24 (D.D.C. 2017).

It is not adequate to rely on policies and procedures that require officials to move such information to official systems within a certain period of time; I exercise and specifically preserve and assert my right to records contained in those files even if material has not yet been moved to official systems or if officials have, through negligence or willfulness, failed to meet their obligations. 

In addition, please note that in conducting a “reasonable search” as required by law, you must employ the most up-to-date technologies and tools available, in addition to searches by individual custodians likely to have responsive information. 

Furthermore, agencies that have adopted the National Archives and Records Agency (NARA) Capstone program, or similar policies, now maintain emails in a form that is reasonably likely to be more complete than individual custodians’ files. For example, a custodian may have deleted a responsive email from his or her email program, but DOJ’s archiving tools would capture that email under Capstone. Accordingly, I insist that the EOIR use the most up-to-date technologies to search for responsive information and take steps to ensure that the most complete repositories of information are searched. I am available to work with you to craft appropriate search terms.

If it is your position that any portion of the requested records is exempt from disclosure, I request that you provide an index of those documents as required under Vaughn v. Rosen, 484 F.2d 820 (D.C. Cir. 1973), cert. denied, 415 U.S. 977 (1974). The index must describe each document claimed as exempt with sufficient specificity “to permit a reasoned judgment as to whether the material is actually exempt under FOIA.” Founding Church of Scientology v. Bell, 603 F.2d 945, 949 (D.C. Cir. 1979). Moreover, the index “must describe each document or portion thereof withheld, and for each withholding it must discuss the consequences of disclosing the sought-after information.” King v. U.S. Dep’t of Justice, 830 F.2d 210, 223–24 (D.C. Cir. 1987). Further, “the withholding agency must supply ‘a relatively detailed justification, specifically identifying the reasons why a particular exemption is relevant and correlating those claims with the particular part of a withheld document to which they apply.’” Id. at 224 (citing Mead Data Central, Inc. v. U.S. Dep’t of the Air Force, 566 F.2d 242, 251 (D.C. Cir. 1977)).

In the event some portions of the requested records are properly exempt from disclosure, please disclose any reasonably segregable non-exempt portions of the requested records. If it is your position that a record contains non-exempt segments, but that those non-exempt segments are so dispersed throughout the document as to make segregation impossible, please state what portion of the document is non-exempt, and how the material is dispersed throughout the document. Mead Data Central, 566 F.2d at 261. Claims of nonsegregability must be made with the same degree of detail as required for claims of exemptions in a Vaughn index. If a request is denied in whole, please state specifically that it is not reasonable to segregate portions of the record for release.

title: Dominant Chronicle

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Dominant Chronicle
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records mentioning, relating to, and/or final products generated by Dominant Chronicle, a joint DIA-FBI analysis program focusing on anti-money laundering efforts as they relate to counterdrug activities, in operation approximately between 1997 and 2000.

Previously released reports describe Dominant Chronicle as a "... foreign document/information exploitation initiative that supports the U.S. counterdrug efforts via multiagency sharing of comprehensive analytical reports derived from documents seized by foreign law enforcement agencies" (https://www.gao.gov/assets/nsiad-98-142.pdf, p. 32); "...the Defense Intelligence Agency-FBI document analysis center in the Washington, D.C. area. Time-sensitive information is isolated and checked against U.S. data bases. The combined ("fused") information is then returned to Mexican authorities to support law enforcement operations, e.g., raids against specific drug trafficking locations. Products from Dominant Chronicle are also provided to Mexican law enforcement with expanded analysis for use in its strategic efforts." (https://www.ojp.gov/pdffiles1/Photocopy/167254NCJRS.pdf, p. 30); " Additionally, the Defense Intelligence Agency hosts and supports the FBI-led Interagency Dominant Chronicle money laundering intelligence program."(https://www.ojp.gov/ondcppubs/publications/pdf/budget98.pdf, p.32)

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.
